title: 2025 Annual Summary: Self-Evolution and Life Echoes
summary: This year, I completed the transition from "technical executor" to "life architect".
markdown:
![image]()
> Keywords of the year: evolution, self-consistency, down-to-earth
## 📊 2025 Annual Data Dashboard
cognitive input
- 🎧 Podcast: 147 days × 108 episodes = 77 hours of cognitive upgrades
- 🎵 Music: 5,524 songs × 509 hours, 54% new songs explored
Habit formation
- 🏃 Pomodoro: 129 times = 42.5 hours of ritual
- 💤 Work and rest rules: go to bed at 12 o'clock, get up at 7 o'clock, consistent throughout the year
health achievement
- 💪 Fatty liver: disappear completely ✓
- 🧘 Peace of mind: full recovery after thyroid surgery
Tool investment
- 🛠️ AI ecosystem: Windsurf, Cursor, Claude, Readdy, Figma, Paraflow
relationship breakthrough
- 💑 Zero quarrels: 365 days a year, achieve qualitative changes in communication with your wife
- 👨‍👦 Parent-child growth: from mutual blame-shifting to two-way apology
creative output
- 🚀 Project Prompt is online
---
## 1. Growth: Cognition and inner transformation
This year, I completed the transition from "technical executor" to "life architect".
- Annual Cognitive Awakening: From Small Universe to "Realistic Life"
- In 2025, "Zhixing Bistro" in the small universe became the driving force for me to break out of the "technical cocoon". It made me realize that finance is no longer a cold number, but a perspective from which to observe life. I deeply understand that "financial management means managing life": every allocation of resources is essentially a vote for the life I want. This cross-border perspective has helped me learn to delay judgment, understand the complexity of the world, and let go of a lot of blind financial anxieties. A total of 108 podcast episodes were listened to over 147 days throughout the year, totaling 77 hours. These sounds accompany me when commuting, walking, and doing housework, turning fragmented time into prime time for cognitive upgrades.
- Challenges and Resilience: From Coder to AI Commander
- The arrival of the AI ​​era brings both challenges and opportunities. This year, I completed the evolution from "letting AI write a line of code" to "commanding AI to complete the entire project." I deeply understand the essence of AI-assisted programming: the ability to ask questions is more important than the ability to code, and the intuition of architecture is more critical than the memory of grammar. This expansion of the boundaries of my abilities gives me the confidence to independently solve life problems and create interesting products. This year is also the year that I truly embraced the AI ​​tool ecosystem. I have subscribed to Windsurf, Cursor, Claude Code Max, Readdy, Figma, Paraflow and other tools. These investments are not only monetary costs, but also a vote of confidence in new era productivity tools.
- Hardcore Warfare: The Birth of Project Prompt
- I personally built and launched this product. My original intention was to transform vague ideas into professional prompt words so that AI can truly understand the product logic. This is not only a tool, but also the ultimate practical implementation of my status as a "full stack creator" in 2025, proving the tremendous productivity generated by the combination of logic and tools.
- A new discovery of self: the "collection" of emotions and the "implementation" of action
- Hold my temper: When facing my wife and children who are closest to me, I learned to "just be reasonable and not lose my temper". What I am most proud of this year is that I have zero quarrels with my wife. This is not to avoid conflicts, but to learn to communicate in a more mature way - listen first before speaking when there are differences, and calm down before expressing emotions. This gentle and firm force makes the family atmosphere more stable and brings the marriage relationship into a new stage.
- Down-to-earth: I gradually came out of the fantasy in the past and let my ideas "feet on the ground". I am becoming more and more clear about the things I really like, and I am no longer disturbed by the outside world. This sense of certainty is my most solid growth this year.
- Two-way growth with children: education is self-cultivation
- This year, the way I interact with my children has undergone a qualitative change. I began to take the initiative to apologize to my children, and my children also learned to take the initiative to apologize. The family is no longer a battlefield where each other shirks responsibilities. My son no longer yells, but has learned to reason with us. This feeling of mutual influence and common growth made me realize that education is not a one-way output, but a two-way practice.
- What makes me even more gratified is seeing the sense of responsibility and initiative in the children. This year he started to read. We only need to say "starting to read" and he will do it consciously. The most unforgettable thing is that before the storytelling competition in kindergarten, we chose the story "The King of Money Ejaculates". The children went into the study room by themselves, listened to the video, and memorized it piece by piece until they memorized the whole story. Although he forgot the last sentence when he was speaking live, he kept pulling us to listen to him during those days until he memorized it all word for word. That persistence for perfection and unwillingness to admit defeat showed me his inner strength.
---
## 2. Life: concrete fireworks and poetry
Life is not about rushing, but about feeling the road.
- Physical and mental state: a "restart" from the inside out
- Health victory: The happiest discovery during the physical examination in 2025 is that the fatty liver has completely disappeared! Although I haven't lost much weight, my belly is obviously smaller. The recovery after thyroid surgery combined with the change in mentality has brought me into a state of peace that I have never experienced before.
- Work and rest concentration: Still maintaining the rhythm of "going to bed at 12 o'clock and getting up at 7 o'clock", combined with exercise every now and then, the sense of control over the body is returning.
- Habit formation: This year I started using Tomato TODO to check in, and developed the habit of listening to podcasts in the morning and taking a twenty-minute walk after lunch. I persisted 129 times throughout the year, totaling 42 hours and 34 minutes. These seemingly small rituals make every day more calm and fulfilling.
- Small blessings in life: "nearby" and "lovers" in the lens
- Music companionship: I listened to a total of 5524 songs this year, a total of 509 hours, and new songs accounted for 54%. Music has become my most loyal companion in life: a pick-me-up during my commute, a background music for late-night work, and a companion for reflection during walks. The proportion of 54% new songs shows that I still remain curious about new things and am willing to step out of my comfort zone to explore unknown melodies.
- Daily life through the lens: After buying an action camera, I fell in love with photography. There are no famous mountains or rivers in my shots, but they are filled with the most precious daily life: my wife’s smiling face, the figures of my children playing, the tree at the door of my house that changes color with the seasons, and the park where I have walked countless times. Photography taught me to stop and observe, and to discover that beauty does not require traveling far, it is in the scenery I pass by every day.
- Walking footsteps: Although I discovered that "beauty does not require traveling far," I did not stop exploring this year. We went to Lishui, Nanjing, Jiaxing, and Shanghai, and each city left our family with laughter and memories. Travel is not about escaping from daily life, but about re-seeing life from a new perspective and then returning to daily life with richer experiences.

## 3. Unfinished business: those regrets and reflections
Real growth includes completed and unfinished things.
- The regret of reading: There are a bunch of books in the favorites that I want to read, but very few of them are actually opened. What separates from "wanting to read" to "finishing reading" is not time, but action.
- Shelving of the guitar: I have barely practiced the fingertip melody I once longed for this year. The guitar sits quietly against the wall, reminding me that some loves require sustained investment to blossom.
- Lack of records: There are too few records of each day. There are many moments that I feel I will remember at the moment, but they become blurry as time goes by. Life needs more "freezing" in order to look back more clearly.
These regrets are not failures, but a starting point for a fresh start in 2026.
---
## 4. Outlook: Prologue to 2026
It’s not just about setting goals, it’s about setting “status.”
- 2026 Keyword of the Year: Growth (Growth & Vitality)
- 2026 is a year of continued strength. I hope that on the soil that will be consolidated in 2025, my career and life will be like plants, with the depth to take root downward and the power to grow upward.
- The "first time" I want to try: from "making functions" to "making products"
- In 2026, I hope to achieve a real leap from "developer" to "product person". No matter which project, my goal is to truly accumulate my own user base for the first time, so that I can better understand how to operate products and create value.
- Ideal life fragment:
- On a weekend afternoon in 2026, I sat at my desk and watched the user feedback growing in the background of the product. The action camera around you is filled with new footage of your family laughing. At that moment, the sense of career achievement and the fireworks of life were perfectly intertwined.
- Message to 2026:
- "Keep your feet on the ground and enjoy the joy of continuous growth. Robin, go create something truly interesting!"
